skill.name: 2agent
skill.description: Configures a 2-Agent workflow that connects Cursor planning with Claude Code implementation work.
skill.summary: Sets up Cursor commands, Claude memory files, rules, and update flows for a 2-Agent development workflow.
skill.author: Chachamaru127

security_audit.summary: Most command-substitution and obfuscation alerts are false positives from documented local shell snippets and Japanese Markdown text. Real concerns remain around hidden harness configuration writes, predictable /tmp usage, executable hook installation, and permissive bypass-mode guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Show the hook contents before installation, ask for explicit consent, and verify the template source before chmod +x is applied.
Set disableBypassPermissionsMode in generated settings by default, or require an explicit user choice before allowing bypassPermissions.
Replace /tmp/existing_tasks.md with mktemp or a project-local temporary file created with restrictive permissions.
List each hidden file before writing, preserve backups, and ask before creating or replacing agent configuration files.

semantic_findings.title: Executable Hook Installation
semantic_findings.description: The setup and update flows copy auto-cleanup-hook.sh into .claude/scripts and make it executable. Agent hook scripts can run later with project permissions, so users need explicit review and consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation directly instructs copying a plugin-provided shell hook and applying chmod +x. The hook content is not shown in these files, so the execution impact cannot be fully verified.

content.value_statement: Teams can lose context when PM planning and implementation happen in different tools. This skill creates Cursor commands and Claude memory files for a 2-Agent workflow.
actual_capabilities: Routes setup, update, and Cursor integration requests to focused sub-skill documents.
Creates Cursor command files for session start, project overview, planning, handoff, and review workflows.
Initializes Claude memory files for session logs, decisions, and reusable project patterns.
Copies Claude workflow rules and coding standards from plugin templates.
Writes version tracking files so future updates can compare installed and plugin versions.
Updates existing workflow files while backing up files and preserving user task content.
limitations: It depends on claude-code-harness templates being installed and available locally.
It modifies hidden project directories such as .claude and .cursor.
It does not replace human review of generated settings, rules, or hook scripts.
It is focused on workflow setup, not full project management or code implementation.

best_practices: Review every hidden configuration file before accepting generated workflow changes.
Back up existing project plans and memory files before running update flows.
Inspect generated hook scripts and permission settings before team rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not run setup in a repository with uncommitted critical planning files and no backup.
Do not enable generated hooks without reading the script behavior first.
Do not treat the workflow files as a substitute for human project ownership.

faq.question: What does this skill set up?
faq.answer: It sets up files for a 2-Agent workflow that connects Cursor planning with Claude Code implementation work.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it write project files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create or update .cursor commands, .claude memory files, rules, scripts, and harness version files.

faq.question: Can it update an existing setup?
faq.answer: Yes. The update flow detects existing files, creates backups, and preserves user task content where supported.

faq.question: Should generated hook scripts be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Hook scripts may run later with project permissions, so review them before enabling them.

faq.question: Is it safe for every repository?
faq.answer: No. It should be used only after reviewing hidden file changes, permission settings, and backup behavior.
